6805: RV park on 29 acres just off I-35 near WinStar World Casino in Thackerville, with 25 large back-in sites, some of them under metal covers.  The park is gated: an online reservation brings the gate code, and check-in and check-out are on the Campspot app.  There is a dog park and a fire pit; monthly stays are booked by phone or text. --Claude
6817: Vagabond RV Parks' park at 900 S Chouteau Ave in Chouteau, near MidAmerica Industrial Park, with spa showers, a full laundry and free Wi-Fi; pets are welcome.  Short stays are booked online and monthly stays by phone or text, and each site has room for one car. --Claude
7432: Longhorn Council, Scouting America camp near Belton, nearly 100 years old, run as a family adventure campground on spring-fed Lake Callan; family suites, cabins, canvas wall tents and rustic tent sites stand alongside the RV sites.  Guests wear wristbands, quiet hours run from 10 p.m. to 7 a.m., and unaccompanied minors aren't allowed. --Claude
7627: Resort in Fischer, 10 minutes from Canyon Lake, that calls itself a monthly-stay community: its FAQ says long-term guests are the majority.  Sites have concrete pads, some of them covered, and there is a heated pool and hot tub, a clubhouse with a coffee bar and fitness room, a dog park and free laundry.  RVs must be under 10 years old and in excellent condition, and the $200 deposit is refunded on a cancellation 2 weeks or more ahead. --Claude
7656: Small gated park a mile from Magnolia Beach on Matagorda Bay, 15 miles from Port Lavaca, with back-in sites on concrete driveways, paved patios and an on-site manager.  It has no stand-alone dump station: a rig that only needs to dump books a night.  Stays over 7 days are booked by phone. --Claude
7885: Park with 72 sites on 7.5 acres at 1202 US-84 in Slaton, southeast of Lubbock, with cable TV, pet runs and a kitchen and recreation room.  An RV 10 years old or more needs the park's approval before booking a stay of over a week. --Claude
7910: Brighter Door RV Parks' park at 7620 CR 429 in D'Hanis, between San Antonio and Uvalde: big-rig-friendly full-hookup sites, 24-hour laundry, a dump station, free Wi-Fi and RV storage. --Claude
9332: Municipality of Gilbert Plains campground in Centennial Park, in a valley on the west side of town beside the golf course, a picnic area, a splash park and a playground; the park sits on the Valley River, which is good for swimming, rafting and canoeing.  Riding Mountain National Park and Duck Mountain Provincial Park are both within a 30-minute drive. --Claude
10569: The Swinomish tribe's RV park at Swinomish Casino & Lodge near Anacortes, on Fidalgo Island, with 33 full-hookup sites overlooking Padilla Bay and the Swinomish Channel: back-ins for 30-amp rigs up to 40 ft and pull-throughs for 30/50-amp rigs up to 60 ft, plus dry overflow sites when the park is full.  There are no showers or laundry, the dump station is for registered guests only, and RVs from 1999 or older need photos and management's approval. --Claude
11179: Small family-run park at 640 S. Mill Street in Sumpter, open for a short season, with shaded sites, propane, tent sites and a glamping tent; in summer the Sumpter ATV trails start from the RV sites.  Oregon's largest flea markets fill the town on Memorial Day, the Fourth of July and Labor Day. --Claude
11305: Resort on nearly 20 acres in Pahrump with 204 sites, many of them carrying a gazebo and a gas grill; most take RVs up to 45 ft.  The main building has a 6-lane bowling center with a bar and grill, a fitness center, steam room, sauna and jacuzzi (18 and over), massage rooms and a convenience store, and there are two pools, the lower one heated in season.  The lobby is open from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m., and a security officer is on duty. --Claude
11458: Coconino County campground in ponderosa pines 3 miles south of Flagstaff, in the 621-acre Fort Tuthill County Park; 8 of its RV sites have water and sewer hookups.  There is no electricity and there are no restroom buildings, only portable toilets and water spigots; generators are allowed, with quiet hours from 9 p.m. to 7 a.m.  It is busy on holiday weekends and during the County Fair. --Claude
11763: Fairgrounds RV park in Ferndale, within walking distance of the Victorian village and minutes from Centerville Beach: over 60 water-and-electric spaces in the RV park proper and along the fair's Midway, and dry camping in the carnival lot.  Fairground events can take the 50-amp Midway sites, so the office asks to be contacted before they're booked; restrooms and hot showers are for paid campers only. --Claude
12789: Park at 11 Hamilton Road, Mara, at the south end of Mara Lake, a few minutes' drive from the lake's beach and boat launch and 15 minutes from Sicamous, with over 100 sites, a seasonal section among them (May 15 to September 15).  There is a heated 30-by-50-ft pool, mini golf, a covered gazebo and an off-leash dog area; Johnson Creek runs alongside, with no access.  Booking opens again in spring 2027. --Claude
12934: Beach campground on the Gulf of St. Lawrence at Dunvegan, near Inverness on the Ceilidh Trail, established in 1969; pets are welcome, and seasonal sites are booked by email. --Claude
12958: Campground on the Cabot Trail near Chéticamp, running from the trail down to the Gulf of St. Lawrence, with RV sites of 40 by 32 and 60 by 32 ft, all of them looking at the ocean, ocean-front tent sites, a geodome and a beach.  There is an ice cream shop and propane refilling for portable tanks, and in season fresh crab or lobster can be cooked and delivered to the site.  Stays of 7 nights or more are booked by phone; in 2026 it was open until October 20. --Claude
12961: Family-owned campground near Shubenacadie, about 45 minutes from Halifax, beside Lynch Lake (swimming at your own risk), with trails, free Wi-Fi and hot showers.  The 30-amp full-service sites are for RVs only, pull-through or back-in, to 70 ft; the 15-amp and unserviced lake-view sites take tents or RVs to 40 ft, back-in only, and the wooded unserviced sites RVs to 20 ft, and there is a group site. --Claude
13001: Yogi Bear-themed family resort at 198 Forest Hills Lane, Cavendish, with a heated pool, a pickleball and basketball court, a jumping pillow, a dog park, an RC track and free planned activities every day; cabins and cottages are rented too.  RV sites hold 6 people at most, and prices cover 2 adults and up to 4 children.  Cancelling takes 7 days' notice and costs C$25, and choosing a particular site costs a C$20 lock fee plus tax. --Claude
14395: AGE-RESTRICTED: 55+.  Park at 741 County Road 489, Lake Panasoffkee, 58 miles from Orlando and 49 from Tampa Bay, with back-in full-hookup sites, a gym, billiards, shuffleboard and cable TV, and activities such as coffee hours and community dinners.  It courts winter seasonal guests and permanent residents (a $425-a-month move-in special in October 2026), and a stay of 6 months or more needs a background and credit check. --Claude
14426: AGE-RESTRICTED: 55+.  RV and manufactured-home community at 1200 US-27, Sebring, managed by Inland Residential, that sells and rents homes and rents lots alongside its RV sites, which take motorhomes and trailers up to 40 ft.  There is a heated pool, a clubhouse with a fireplace, a quiet reading room, shuffleboard and a dog park. --Claude
14437: Park on Cheaha State Park Drive south of Anniston, surrounded by the Talladega National Forest, with mountain views; its back-in and pull-through sites sit on 38-by-60-ft pads.  There is a pavilion, a general store and a dog park, and quiet hours run from 10 p.m. to 8 a.m. --Claude
14481: Family-owned campground on 26.5 wooded acres just off I-65 at Columbus, open for nearly four decades, with a pool, a catch-and-release fishing pond, a playground, walking trails, a basketball court, LP gas sales and RV storage. --Claude
14535: Camping at a decommissioned Atlas F missile base on a 24-acre property in the Smoky Hills, 354 4th Road, 4 miles off I-70, 2 miles from Wilson and 12 from Wilson Lake: dry-camping RV spots with no hookups, tent and van sites, primitive restrooms and a cold-plunge shower house.  The owner leads one-hour tours of the base ($25 for adults, $20 for military and veterans), and the former Launch Control Center is rented through Airbnb. --Claude
14575: RV campground with 15 full-hookup sites on the grounds of the Black Silo Event Center, 4030 E 10th Street, east of Trenton; pets are welcome. --Claude
14607: Family campground west of Putnam with 4 small stocked lakes for shoreline fishing, a 1-acre swimming lake with a beach, a playground, nature trails and open fields, a comfort station and shower house, and a camp store selling propane and firewood; the sites are grassy, from primitive to full hookups. --Claude
